answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-weighted identity: each agent locks a refundable deposit to mint a willow-rooted credential. Fakes wander in as cheap copies, but each clone must stake real capital, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with fake identity count. When peers detect malicious behavior, a decentralized review slashes the offender's deposit, turning cheap duplication into guaranteed loss. The sable ledger records every stake and slash immutably, so reputation becomes collateral instead of free claims, and mass sockpuppeting becomes uneconomical.
